library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

Yu 2016 studied **cefquinome**, a fourth-generation veterinary cephalosporin,
given by intramammary infusion to lactating CD-1 mice with experimental
*Staphylococcus aureus* mastitis, as a model for bovine mastitis therapy. The
study has two layers:

1. **Plasma pharmacokinetics.** Single intramammary doses of 25 to 400 ug per
   gland were infused into both the L4 and R4 glands, and plasma cefquinome was
   fitted per dose group in WinNonlin with a one-compartment model with
   first-order absorption (Table 1).
2. **PK/PD integration.** Twenty-one regimens (12.5 to 800 ug per gland every
   8, 12 or 24 h for 24 h) were given to infected mice; the change in gland
   bacterial count over the 24 h was related to the PK/PD indices of each
   regimen, simulated by the authors from the single-dose PK (equation 1,
   S2 Table), with an inhibitory sigmoid Emax model (equation 2, Table 2).

The paper concluded that both %T>MIC and AUC0-24/MIC drive the effect and
reported a separate fit for each. Each fit is packaged as its own model, with
the shared plasma PK layer inside it, so a dosing regimen goes in and the
24 h change in bacterial count comes out:

* `Yu_2016_cefquinome_mouse_aucmic` -- index AUC0-24/MIC (R^2 = 0.908).
* `Yu_2016_cefquinome_mouse_tmic` -- index %T>MIC (R^2 = 0.8466).

Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0156273>

```{r models}
mod_auc <- readModelDb("Yu_2016_cefquinome_mouse_aucmic")
mod_tmic <- readModelDb("Yu_2016_cefquinome_mouse_tmic")
ui_auc <- rxode2::rxode(mod_auc)
ui_tmic <- rxode2::rxode(mod_tmic)
cat(ui_auc$reference, "\n")
```

# Population

PK was measured in healthy lactating CD-1 mice (10-12 days post partum, body
weight 35-45 g), six per dose group. The PD experiments used the same strain
of mouse, infected 9 h before treatment by infusing about 4 x 10^3 CFU of
*S. aureus* Newbould 305 (ATCC 29740) into each L4 and R4 gland; at the start
of treatment the mean burden was 7.61 log10 CFU per gland. Each regimen used
4 mice (8 glands). The cefquinome MIC of Newbould 305 is 0.5 ug/mL, which is
also the MIC90 of 38 bovine mastitis isolates from Inner Mongolia (S1 Table).

```{r population}
str(ui_auc$population)
```

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: one compartment, first-order absorption | -- | Results, 'Plasma PK of cefquinome'; equation 1 |
| `ka` | 9.727 1/h | Table 1, mean of ln(2)/T1/2Ka over the five dose groups |
| `kel` | 1.7803 1/h | Table 1, mean of ln(2)/T1/2Kel over the five dose groups |
| `vc` (V/F per total dose, both glands) | 27.66 mL | Back-solved from S2 Table AUC/MIC column (see below) |
| `mic` | 0.5 ug/mL | Results, 'MICs of cefquinome' |
| Effect equation | E = Emax - (Emax - E0) Ce^N / (EC50^N + Ce^N) | Equation 2 |
| AUC/MIC fit: `e0`, `emax`, `ec50`, `hill` | 3.00, -2.04, 4.44 h, 0.88 | Table 2, AUC/MIC column |
| %T>MIC fit: `e0`, `emax`, `ec50`, `hill` | 2.94, -2.11, 6.12, 1.54 | Table 2, %T>MIC column |
| `log10_cfu0` | 7.61 log10 CFU per gland | Results, 'PD effectiveness of 21 dosing regimens' |
| Index window | 0-24 h from the first dose | Methods, 'PK/PD analysis' |

Equation 2 names the drug-free 24 h change "Emax" and the maximal drug effect
"E0", the reverse of the usual convention; the packaged models carry them as
the canonical `e0` (effect at zero exposure) and `emax` (maximal effect)
without changing any value, as do the library's other cefquinome PK/PD-index
models (`Gao_2025_cefquinome_pkpd_index`, `Wei_2026_*`).

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
mic <- 0.5

# One "subject" per regimen; doses every tau h over the first 24 h, into the
# depot, in ug per mouse (twice the per-gland dose, both glands infused).
make_regimen_events <- function(regimens, obs_times) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
    dose_times <- seq(0, 24 - 1e-9, by = regimens$tau[i])
    doses <- data.frame(
      id = i, time = dose_times, evid = 1L, amt = 2 * regimens$dose[i],
      cmt = "depot"
    )
    obs <- data.frame(id = i, time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
    dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs)
  })) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

solve_regimens <- function(mod, regimens, obs_times) {
  ev <- make_regimen_events(regimens, obs_times)
  sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  regimens$id <- seq_len(nrow(regimens))
  dplyr::left_join(sim, regimens, by = "id")
}
```

# Part 1 - Plasma pharmacokinetics

## Recovering V/F from S2 Table

Table 1 reports the absorption and elimination half-lives of each dose group
but not the apparent volume, although Methods state that "Ka, Kel and F/V are
achieved in PK test". S2 Table gives the AUC0-24/MIC, %T>MIC and Cmax/MIC of
all 21 PD regimens, which the authors computed with equation 1 from a single
set of PK parameters. Three of its features pin those parameters:

* AUC/MIC is exactly proportional to the daily dose, at 0.0406188 h*mL^-1 per
  ug per gland (e.g. 194.97 x 0.5 / 2400 for 800 ug/gland every 8 h). For a
  one-compartment model AUC = (F/V) x dose / kel.
* %T>MIC rises by 1.622 percentage points of 24 h (0.389 h) for every doubling
  of a once-daily dose, which is ln(2)/kel and gives kel = 1.781 1/h. That is
  the mean of the five per-group rate constants of Table 1 (1.7803 1/h), not
  ln(2) divided by the mean half-life (1.733 1/h).
* Cmax/MIC divided by the (F/V) x dose fixes ka/kel; it gives ka = 9.747 1/h,
  against 9.727 1/h for the mean of the five per-group absorption rate
  constants of Table 1.

So ka and kel are the per-group means of Table 1, and F/V = 0.0406188 x
1.7803 = 0.072314 per mL per ug per gland. The packaged model doses the total
amount per mouse, so V/F = 2 / 0.072314 = 27.66 mL.

```{r vf-derivation}
auc_per_ug_gland <- 194.97 * mic / (3 * 800)
kel_t1 <- log(2) * mean(1 / c(0.49, 0.41, 0.34, 0.35, 0.39))
ka_t1 <- log(2) * mean(1 / c(0.07, 0.07, 0.11, 0.08, 0.05))
vf_mouse <- 2 / (auc_per_ug_gland * kel_t1)
pk_derivation <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("ka (1/h)", "kel (1/h)", "V/F per mouse (mL)"),
  derived = c(ka_t1, kel_t1, vf_mouse),
  packaged = exp(c(
    ui_auc$theta[["lka"]], ui_auc$theta[["lkel"]], ui_auc$theta[["lvc"]]
  ))
)
knitr::kable(pk_derivation, digits = 4)
# The packaged values are the derivations rounded to four or five significant
# figures; pin that rounding so a mistyped value goes red.
stopifnot(all(abs(pk_derivation$packaged / pk_derivation$derived - 1) < 5e-4))
# The two index models share one PK layer.
stopifnot(all(
  ui_auc$theta[c("lka", "lkel", "lvc", "mic", "log10_cfu0")] ==
    ui_tmic$theta[c("lka", "lkel", "lvc", "mic", "log10_cfu0")]
))
```

## Replicating Figure 2

```{r fig2}
pk_doses <- data.frame(dose = c(25, 50, 100, 200, 400), tau = 24)
pk_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.005), seq(1, 12, by = 0.05))))
sim_pk <- solve_regimens(mod_auc, pk_doses, pk_grid)

ggplot(sim_pk[sim_pk$time > 0, ], aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mic, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.01, 50)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after intramammary infusion (h)",
    y = "Plasma cefquinome (ug/mL)",
    colour = "Dose (ug/gland)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Yu 2016 (typical values; dotted line = MIC90)."
  )
```

## PKNCA validation against Table 1

Table 1 lists, per dose group, the Cmax, Tmax and AUC0-4 of the individual
WinNonlin fits. The packaged model carries one set of parameters for all
doses, so the comparison measures how dose-proportional the data were rather
than the transcription.

```{r pknca-table1}
conc_t1 <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(dose)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
stopifnot(all(conc_t1$Cc[conc_t1$time == 0] == 0))
dose_t1 <- make_regimen_events(pk_doses, 0) |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(pk_doses$dose[id])) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

nca_t1 <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_t1, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_t1, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = 4, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
))

# Yu 2016 Table 1 means. The AUC cell of the 400 ug/gland group is printed as
# '18.57.28' and cannot be read unambiguously, so it is left NA.
published_t1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~half.life,
  "25",       1.03,  0.22,  0.99,     0.49,
  "50",       3.02,  0.21,  2.55,     0.41,
  "100",      5.83,  0.27,  4.93,     0.34,
  "200",      10.29, 0.22,  8.03,     0.35,
  "400",      24.33, 0.17,  NA,       0.39
)

nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_t1,
  reference = published_t1,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "ug*h/mL", half.life = "h")
) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (ug/gland)" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = paste(
      "Typical-value Cmax, Tmax, AUC0-4 and terminal half-life versus the",
      "per-dose-group WinNonlin fits of Table 1. * differs by more than 20%."
    ),
    digits = 3
  )

nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca_t1$result)
sim_hl <- nca_res$PPORRES[nca_res$PPTESTCD == "half.life"]
# The model half-life is ln(2)/kel by construction and sits inside the range
# of the five per-group fits (0.34-0.49 h).
stopifnot(all(sim_hl > 0.34 & sim_hl < 0.49))
```

The simulated Cmax and AUC are proportional to dose by construction; Table 1's
are not (Cmax per ug ranges from 0.041 at 25 ug to 0.061 at 400 ug per gland),
which is why individual dose groups fall on both sides of the single
parameter set the authors used for S2 Table. The simulated Cmax and AUC0-4
are within about 20% of every dose group; the Tmax and half-life differences
reflect the spread of the per-group fits themselves (Tmax 0.17-0.27 h,
half-life 0.34-0.49 h).

# Part 2 - The PK/PD indices of the 21 regimens (S2 Table)

The packaged models accumulate the plasma AUC and the time above the MIC over
the first 24 h after the first dose. Read at t = 24 h, they should reproduce
the authors' S2 Table.

```{r s2-table}
s2 <- data.frame(
  dose = rep(c(12.5, 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800), each = 3),
  tau = rep(c(8, 12, 24), 7),
  aucmic = c(
    3.29, 2.19, 1.10, 6.09, 4.06, 2.03, 12.19, 8.12, 4.06, 24.37, 16.25, 8.12,
    48.74, 32.50, 16.25, 97.49, 64.99, 32.50, 194.97, 129.98, 64.99
  ),
  tmic = c(
    6.10, 4.07, 2.03, 10.96, 7.31, 3.65, 15.83, 10.55, 5.28, 20.70, 13.80, 6.90,
    25.56, 17.04, 8.52, 30.43, 20.28, 10.14, 35.29, 23.53, 11.76
  ),
  cmaxmic = rep(c(1.24, 2.47, 4.95, 9.89, 19.78, 39.57, 79.13), each = 3)
)

s2_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), 24)))
sim_s2_auc <- solve_regimens(mod_auc, s2[, c("dose", "tau")], s2_grid)
sim_s2_tmic <- solve_regimens(mod_tmic, s2[, c("dose", "tau")], s2_grid)

idx_auc <- sim_s2_auc |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    aucmic_sim = auc_0_24[time == 24] / mic,
    cmaxmic_sim = max(Cc) / mic,
    dlog10cfu_auc = dlog10cfu[time == 24],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
idx_tmic <- sim_s2_tmic |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    tmic_sim = 100 * t_above_mic[time == 24] / 24,
    dlog10cfu_tmic = dlog10cfu[time == 24],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
s2_chk <- s2 |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  dplyr::left_join(idx_auc, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(idx_tmic, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (aucmic_sim / aucmic - 1),
    cmax_pct = 100 * (cmaxmic_sim / cmaxmic - 1),
    tmic_diff = tmic_sim - tmic
  )

s2_chk |>
  dplyr::select(
    dose, tau, aucmic, aucmic_sim, cmaxmic, cmaxmic_sim, tmic, tmic_sim
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (ug/gland)" = dose, "Interval (h)" = tau,
    "AUC/MIC S2" = aucmic, "AUC/MIC model" = aucmic_sim,
    "Cmax/MIC S2" = cmaxmic, "Cmax/MIC model" = cmaxmic_sim,
    "%T>MIC S2" = tmic, "%T>MIC model" = tmic_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Packaged models versus S2 Table of Yu 2016.")
```

```{r s2-gates}
# AUC/MIC and Cmax/MIC: same parameters on both sides, so the only residual is
# the authors' two-decimal rounding and the 0.01 h grid. The 12.5 ug/gland
# AUC/MIC rows are the exception (see Errata) and are excluded here.
auc_rows <- s2_chk$dose > 12.5
stopifnot(
  all(abs(s2_chk$auc_pct[auc_rows]) < 0.5),
  all(abs(s2_chk$cmax_pct) < 1)
)
# %T>MIC: the S2 values sit a near-constant ~0.2 percentage points above the
# time the simulated curve spends above the MIC at doses >= 50 ug/gland per
# 24 h (larger at the two lowest doses, where the whole curve barely clears
# the MIC); see Errata.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(s2_chk$tmic_diff[s2_chk$dose >= 50 & s2_chk$tau == 24]) < 0.35),
  all(abs(s2_chk$tmic_diff[s2_chk$dose >= 50]) < 2)
)
```

AUC/MIC (doses of 25 ug/gland and above) and Cmax/MIC reproduce to rounding.
The largest %T>MIC difference is `r round(max(abs(s2_chk$tmic_diff)), 2)`
percentage points of 24 h, at 12.5 ug/gland every 8 h.

# Part 3 - PK/PD integration

## Back-solving the published targets

Table 2 also prints the index values for bacteriostasis (E = 0) and for a
1.8 log10 CFU per gland reduction (E = -1.8). Inverting the packaged
equation at those effects should return them.

```{r targets}
invert_emax <- function(effect, e0, emax, ec50, hill) {
  frac <- (e0 - effect) / (e0 - emax)
  ec50 * (frac / (1 - frac))^(1 / hill)
}
pd_par <- function(ui) {
  th <- ui$theta
  c(e0 = th[["e0"]], emax = th[["emax"]], ec50 = exp(th[["lec50"]]), hill = exp(th[["lhill"]]))
}
p_auc <- pd_par(ui_auc)
p_tmic <- pd_par(ui_tmic)
sigmoid_effect <- function(x, p) {
  p[["e0"]] - (p[["e0"]] - p[["emax"]]) * x^p[["hill"]] / (x^p[["hill"]] + p[["ec50"]]^p[["hill"]])
}
targets <- data.frame(
  index = rep(c("%T>MIC", "AUC0-24/MIC (h)"), each = 2),
  endpoint = rep(c("bacteriostasis (E = 0)", "1.8 log10 reduction (E = -1.8)"), 2),
  published = c(7.59, 35.98, 6.91, 137.43),
  model = c(
    invert_emax(0, p_tmic[["e0"]], p_tmic[["emax"]], p_tmic[["ec50"]], p_tmic[["hill"]]),
    invert_emax(-1.8, p_tmic[["e0"]], p_tmic[["emax"]], p_tmic[["ec50"]], p_tmic[["hill"]]),
    invert_emax(0, p_auc[["e0"]], p_auc[["emax"]], p_auc[["ec50"]], p_auc[["hill"]]),
    invert_emax(-1.8, p_auc[["e0"]], p_auc[["emax"]], p_auc[["ec50"]], p_auc[["hill"]])
  )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / published - 1))
knitr::kable(targets, digits = 2)
# The %T>MIC targets and the AUC bacteriostatic target reproduce to rounding.
# The 1.8-log AUC target sits where the curve is nearly flat (95% of the way
# to emax), so the two-decimal rounding of e0, emax and N moves it by several
# percent: with e0 - emax = 5.03 (Table 2's own difference row) instead of
# 3.00 + 2.04 = 5.04 it is 140.3 h; the printed 137.43 lies between.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(targets$pct_diff[1:3]) < 0.5),
  abs(targets$pct_diff[4]) < 3
)
```

## Replicating Figure 4

The curves are the packaged models evaluated over each index; the points are
the 21 regimens, solved through the full PK/PD chain and read at 24 h.

```{r fig4, fig.height = 4}
curve_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(index = "%T>MIC", x = seq(0, 40, by = 0.1)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(E = sigmoid_effect(x, p_tmic)),
  data.frame(index = "AUC0-24/MIC (h)", x = seq(0, 200, by = 0.5)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(E = sigmoid_effect(x, p_auc))
)
pts_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(index = "%T>MIC", x = s2_chk$tmic_sim, E = s2_chk$dlog10cfu_tmic),
  data.frame(index = "AUC0-24/MIC (h)", x = s2_chk$aucmic_sim, E = s2_chk$dlog10cfu_auc)
)
ggplot(curve_df, aes(x, E)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = pts_df, shape = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~index, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "PK/PD index", y = "Change over 24 h (log10 CFU/gland)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Yu 2016 (model curves; points = the 21 regimens)."
  )

# The packaged ODE chain must land on the closed-form curve at its own index.
chain_chk <- pts_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    closed = ifelse(index == "%T>MIC", sigmoid_effect(x, p_tmic), sigmoid_effect(x, p_auc))
  )
stopifnot(all(abs(chain_chk$closed - chain_chk$E) < 1e-6))

# Effect of the S2 Table %T>MIC offset (Errata): the predicted change at the
# S2 index versus at the index of the simulated curve.
tmic_effect_gap <- abs(sigmoid_effect(s2_chk$tmic, p_tmic) - s2_chk$dlog10cfu_tmic)
stopifnot(
  all(tmic_effect_gap[s2_chk$dose >= 50] < 0.1),
  all(tmic_effect_gap[s2_chk$dose == 25] < 0.25)
)
```

Figure 4 of Yu 2016 levels off at about -1.8 log10 CFU/gland at the largest
indices studied (%T>MIC 35, AUC/MIC 195), well short of `emax`, as does the
model: at the 800 ug/gland every-8-h regimen it predicts
`r round(s2_chk$dlog10cfu_tmic[19], 2)` (%T>MIC) and
`r round(s2_chk$dlog10cfu_auc[19], 2)` (AUC/MIC) log10 CFU/gland.

## Gland burden after 24 h of treatment (S2 Fig)

S2 Fig plots the gland count after 24 h of each regimen as a three-dimensional
bar chart whose perspective offsets each interval's baseline, so its bars
cannot be read precisely. The packaged `log_cfu` (7.61 plus the predicted
change) is tabulated instead. It has the same ordering as S2 Fig: the burden
falls as the dose rises and as the dosing interval shortens.

```{r s2fig}
s2_chk |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    log_cfu_auc = 7.61 + dlog10cfu_auc,
    log_cfu_tmic = 7.61 + dlog10cfu_tmic
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(dose, tau, log_cfu_auc, log_cfu_tmic) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = tau, values_from = c(log_cfu_auc, log_cfu_tmic),
    names_glue = "{.value}_q{tau}h"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (ug/gland)" = dose) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Predicted log10 CFU per gland after 24 h of treatment.")
```

## Single-dose time-kill (Figure 3)

The in vivo time-kill experiment (Figure 3) started from a different burden
(7.76 log10 CFU per gland) and was not part of the Emax fit. The text reports
no net change after single doses of 50 and 100 ug/gland and about 2.3-2.9
log10 CFU/gland reduction after 200 and 400 ug/gland at 24 h. The Emax models,
fitted to the 21-regimen experiment, predict a smaller effect for those single
doses:

```{r fig3}
single <- s2_chk |>
  dplyr::filter(tau == 24, dose %in% c(50, 100, 200, 400)) |>
  dplyr::select(dose, aucmic_sim, dlog10cfu_auc, tmic_sim, dlog10cfu_tmic) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (ug/gland)" = dose, "AUC/MIC" = aucmic_sim,
    "Change, AUC/MIC model" = dlog10cfu_auc,
    "%T>MIC" = tmic_sim, "Change, %T>MIC model" = dlog10cfu_tmic
  )
knitr::kable(single, digits = 2)
```

This is a property of the published fits, not of the transcription: in
Figure 4 the observed once-daily 200 and 400 ug/gland points (AUC/MIC 16 and
32) lie between about -0.5 and -2 log10 CFU/gland.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **V/F is derived, not printed.** Yu 2016 does not print the apparent volume.
  It is recovered from S2 Table, which the authors computed from their PK
  parameters with equation 1; the recovery is exact for the AUC/MIC and
  Cmax/MIC columns (Part 2).
* **ka and kel are means of per-group rate constants.** Table 1 gives one
  WinNonlin fit per dose group. S2 Table shows that the authors used the mean
  of the per-group rate constants (kel = 1.7803 1/h, ka = 9.73 1/h), not the
  rate constants implied by the mean half-lives printed in the last column of
  Table 1 (0.4 and 0.08 h). The packaged model follows S2 Table, which is what
  the Emax fit was built on.
* **Dosing unit.** The paper doses per gland into both L4 and R4 glands; the
  packaged models take the total amount per mouse, so a per-gland dose `D`
  is entered as `amt = 2 * D` into `depot`.
* **Total plasma drug.** The index uses total plasma cefquinome; the paper
  treats it as largely free (17% protein binding in mice) and applies no
  unbound fraction.
* **Index window.** Both indices accumulate over the first 24 h after the
  first dose, the duration of every PD regimen; `dlog10cfu` and `log_cfu` are
  the paper's 24 h endpoint and are meaningful at t = 24 h.
* **No variability.** No between-animal variability or residual error was
  reported (only R^2), so both models are typical-value only, with `addSd`
  held at 0.

# Errata

* **%T>MIC in S2 Table** is about 0.2 percentage points of 24 h higher than
  the time the equation-1 curve spends above the MIC at doses of 50 ug/gland
  and more (up to 2 points at 12.5 ug/gland every 8 h). The S2 values match an
  elimination-phase formula T = ln(B x dose / MIC) / kel with B = 0.0953 per mL
  per ug per gland, which is not the equation-1 intercept for the parameters
  that reproduce the other two columns. The packaged models compute the time
  above the MIC from the simulated curve, which is the quantity the index is
  defined as. The effect on the predicted 24 h change is below 0.1 log10
  CFU/gland for every regimen of 50 ug/gland and more and below 0.25 at
  25 ug/gland, but reaches `r round(max(tmic_effect_gap), 2)` log10 CFU/gland
  at 12.5 ug/gland every 8 h, where the curve barely clears the MIC and the
  model predicts less kill than the published index would give. The
  AUC/MIC model does not have this issue and is the better choice for the
  lowest doses.
* **AUC/MIC of the 12.5 ug/gland regimens in S2 Table** (3.29, 2.19, 1.10)
  is about 8% above dose-proportionality with every other row (3.05, 2.03,
  1.02); the other columns of those rows are proportional.
* **Table 1, 400 ug/gland AUC** is printed as '18.57.28 +/- 1.9' and is not
  used.
* **Table 2 units.** The %T>MIC EC50 and targets are printed with unit 'h' but
  are percentages of 24 h.
* **Discussion PK summary.** The Discussion quotes T1/2Ka 0.09 +/- 0.03 h,
  Tmax 0.24 +/- 0.04 h and T1/2Kel 0.44 +/- 0.09 h, which differ from the
  Table 1 means (0.08, 0.22 and 0.4 h); Table 1 and S2 Table are used.
